question: A, B, C, D, E, F and G are of different heights. A is taller than only two people. D is shorter than only G. F is taller than A but shorter than B. C is shorter than E. How many people are shorter than E?
solution:
Given: A, B, C, D, E, F, and G are of different heights.

1) A is taller than only two people.

__ > __ > __ > __ > A > __ > __

2) D is shorter than only G.

G > D > __ > __ > A > __ > __

3) F is taller than A but shorter than B.

G > D > B > F > A > __ > __

4) C is shorter than E.

G > D > B > F > A > E > C

So, only one person is shorter than E

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 3".
